AI Software Engineer Intern 
Technical Pre-Assessment

Objective 
Build a small AI-powered document intelligence system that accepts documents, extracts useful information, answers 
questions about the document, and provides evidence for its answers. 
Candidate Task 
You will build a simple web application where a user can: 
1. Upload a PDF/TXT document 
2. Extract and process the document text 
3. Split the text into meaningful chunks 
4. Generate embeddings 
5. Store embeddings in a vector database 
6. Ask questions about the uploaded document 
7. Retrieve the most relevant chunks 
8. Generate an answer using an LLM 
9. Display the answer together with the relevant source chunks 
Recommended Stack 
You are free to choose your own implementation, but we recommend: 
• Backend: Python + FastAPI

Recommended Stack 
You are free to choose your own implementation, but we recommend: 
• Backend: Python + FastAPI 
• AI / ML: OpenAI API / Gemini API / another LLM API 
• Embeddings: OpenAI embeddings / Sentence Transformers 
• Vector DB: FAISS / ChromaDB 
• Frontend: React / Next.js 
• Docker (bonus) 
Core Requirements 
1. Document Processing 
The system should: 
• Accept PDF or TXT files 
• Extract text 
• Clean the extracted text

• Split it into chunks 
• Store metadata such as page number / chunk ID 
2. Semantic Search 
When the user asks a question, for example: 
User: 
What are the main objectives of this research? 
The application should follow this pipeline: 
Question 
 ↓ 
Embedding 
 ↓ 
Vector Search 
 ↓ 
Top relevant chunks 
 ↓ 
LLM 
 ↓ 
Answer + Sources 
3. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) 
You must implement a basic Retrieval Augmented Generation pipeline. The LLM should answer based primarily on the 
retrieved document context. The system should avoid confidently inventing information that isn't present in the document. 
4. Source Attribution 
Example expected output: 
Answer: 

The research focuses on improving retinal disease 
classification using deep learning models. 

Sources:

The research focuses on improving retinal disease 
classification using deep learning models. 

Sources: 

Page 2 
"...the objective of this study is..." 

Page 4 
"...deep learning-based classification..." 
This is particularly useful for evaluating whether you understand practical AI systems, rather than simply calling an LLM 
API. 
Bonus Tasks (Optional) 
The following are not mandatory but will be viewed favorably if attempted.

Bonus 1: Conversation Memory 
Allow the system to understand follow-up questions in context of the previous question, for example: 
User: What is the research about? 
AI: ...

User: Who proposed this approach? 
AI: ... 
Bonus 2: Hybrid Search 
Combine semantic search with keyword search and compare the results. 
Bonus 3: Evaluation 
Create 5–10 predefined questions and evaluate retrieval accuracy, answer relevance, hallucination rate, and latency. 
Bonus 4: Streaming 
Stream the LLM response to the frontend. 
Bonus 5: Docker 
Provide a docker-compose.yml so the complete application can be started with a single command. 
Submission Instructions 
• Push your code to a public GitHub repository 
• Include a README with setup instructions and a short explanation of your design decisions 
• Submit your repository link before the deadline communicated to you separately

Submission Deadline 
• 
Deadline: 18 August 2026, 12:00 AM (midnight) 
• 
Submission: Please send your GitHub repository link to hr@niduslab.com.
